issue.title: Double `pytest.skip` leads to failure

labels.name: type: bug
labels.description: problem that needs to be addressed

labels.name: topic: tracebacks
labels.description: related to displaying and handling of tracebacks

labels.name: type: regression
labels.description: indicates a problem that was introduced in a release which was working previously

issue.body:
Hello everyone.

I think the following is a bug.
```python
@pytest.fixture
def fixA():
    yield
    pytest.skip(reason="A")

@pytest.fixture
def fixB():
    yield
    pytest.skip(reason="B")

def test_skip(fixA, fixB):  # FAILS
    assert True
```
Gives the following error report (removed tracebacks).
```pycon
____________________________ ERROR at teardown of test_skip _____________________________
  + Exception Group Traceback (most recent call last):
  | <traceback>
  | BaseExceptionGroup: errors while tearing down <Function test_skip> (2 sub-exceptions)
  +-+---------------- 1 ----------------
    | <traceback>
    | Skipped: A
    +---------------- 2 ----------------
    | <traceback>
    | Skipped: B
    +------------------------------------
```

Maybe `pytest` checks for the error raised being of the type of skips, and thus here it bugs because it's an `ExceptionGroup` and not a skip type? I'm just very wildly guessing, I don't know the internals of pytest.

comments.body:
In pytest 7.2.2 (or when removing `fixB`), this results in `1 passed, 1 skipped` (which is somewhat confusing but another long-standing issue).

With pytest 7.3.0 and later, this errors in the same way you mention. Bisected to 3a68c08426326e6c8129e94f98d263131da9a032:

- #10226

And I think your guess is spot-on, e.g. around here:

https://github.com/pytest-dev/pytest/blob/b3ee80b62db73b3c6058d27e3b1375c2d52951dc/src/_pytest/runner.py#L398-L410

I suspect this might also happen with other outcome exceptions. Maybe we should immediately raise the first outcome exception as a special case rather than grouping those? Perhaps conditionally as long as there are no other non-outcome exceptions that happened?

cc @Zac-HD @jakkdl who did a lot of work around exception groups
We should consider exception group's with only skip as skip

Ok great!

> Maybe we should immediately raise the first outcome exception as a special case rather than grouping those? Perhaps conditionally as long as there are no other non-outcome exceptions that happened?

I was thinking about this and I don't think the desired behaviour is trivial to define. For example, we might want to skip if there are only skips, but we might also want to allow fixtures to skip even if an inner fixture failed? Like a kind of "catching fixture". It seems far fetched, but I think there's potentially something to clarify here.

Also, we might want to skip at the first skip encountered, OR we might want to allow outermost fixture to still fail the test even if an inner fixture skipped it?

So as I see it, it's a discussion that needs to happen.

The groupings was added so exceptions no longer get lost 

Now we need to account for that in places

I did a quick excursion to exitstack

Exitstack nests the errors by manipulation of the context so it behaves as if it was nested 

We should consider whether we want that or groups in general 

Based on the behavior of exception groups i slightly prefer the idea of eventually handling those from groups
We'll need to handle `ExceptionGroup`s anyway, in case the user calls `pytest.skip()` from inside an asyncio.TaskGroup context manager (among other cases)

would love to take a crack at this now that i've made some progress with pytest.exit().
